facts.rationale: Corrects the idealized descending-sort description with the actual fixed-i sentinel data flow.
facts.value: Enumerates fighter identifiers through mnDiagram_GetFighterByIndex. Unlocked entries receive the fighter-mode statistic in xC and zero in x8; locked entries receive -1 in both halves. It scans later non-sentinel entries, selecting larger values unless entries[i] is sentinel, in which case every later valid entry replaces maxIdx. The selected entry is inserted at i by shifting intervening entries. entries[rank] then yields its identifier or SELKIND_COUNT, and Diagram3 consumes the identifier for its fighter row.

evidence.why: Sentinel setup, fixed-i disjunct, shifting and unchecked return.

facts.rationale: Explicitly corrects the false unconditional tie-stability and descending-order claims.
facts.value: The query mutates only its local ranking array. Locked fighters are marked with the all-ones value and ignored as scan candidates. With a valid current entry, strict greater-than maximum selection and insertion shifts preserve equal-value order. With an unavailable current entry, however, the disjunct tests entries[i] throughout the scan, so the last subsequent valid entry is selected regardless of value; stable descending ordering is not generally guaranteed. A sentinel-valued requested entry returns SELKIND_COUNT. rank is not bounds checked.

evidence.why: Exact branch structure and fallthrough.
Conditional reclamation deferral.

facts.rationale: Adds the meaningful destruction-to-arrow fallthrough and avoids an unsupported unconditional immediate-teardown interpretation.
facts.value: When shared menu byte 0 is 0x1E and byte 0x10 is 1, the callback updates navigation arrows. When menu byte 0 remains 0x1E but byte 0x10 is not 1, it requests destruction of the GObj and then falls through to the same arrow update; there is no return after that request. When the menu byte differs from 0x1E, it removes the globally tracked process, installs OnAnimComplete, copies the scheduler flag, hides the joint at user-data pointer slot 4, removes and nulls header_text, and returns without updating arrows. Generic GObj destruction can defer reclamation for its protected current object; this routine itself does not prove that every invocation is protected.

facts.rationale: Separates back from neighboring-page behavior and retains the exceptional nonanimated destruction/fallthrough path.
facts.value: Maintains fighter and name modes with separate selected indices, a scroll offset and ten visible rows. Directional input uses mode-specific limits; mode toggling rejects zero names and resets an excessive fighter-mode scroll to zero. Back saves selections/mode, requests menu transition (0x1C,0,3), and clears rows. Adjacent-page input saves state, clears rows, destroys the separate input GObj, and initializes Diagram1 or Diagram3. The display callback updates arrows while menu byte 0 is 0x1E and byte 0x10 is 1; a same-menu non-1 state requests destruction and still falls through to arrow updates, while a different menu installs animated teardown and returns.
